shortlist.label: Anal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recent rectal bleeding and a 20-year history of a slowly enlarging anal mass

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm and fibrotic consistency of the lesion, which is consistent with a smooth muscle tumor

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm and fibrotic consistency of the lesion, which could also be consistent with a benign fat tumor

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed and covered by regular skin, which is consistent with a benign cystic lesion

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm and fibrotic consistency of the lesion, which is consistent with a benign fibrous tumor

raw.rationale: The lesion's firm and fibrotic consistency, non-tender nature, and well-circumscribed appearance are consistent with a leiomyoma, a type of smooth muscle tumor that can occur in the anal canal.

rejected.label: Anal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of bleeding or discharge and the lesion's firm, fibrotic consistency are not typical of adenocarcinoma, which is often more aggressive and ulcerated.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically soft and mobile, which does not match the firm and fibrotic consistency of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Epidermoid cysts are usually fluctuant and may have a visible opening or expressible contents, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: While fibroma could be considered due to the fibrotic nature of the lesion, leiomyoma is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the clinical and gross findings.
